executive_summary.conclusion: DuckDB clearly exposes its analytical database offer, license and current installation route. The main observed obstacle is localized to Python LTS onboarding: the LTS documentation uses an unpinned install command and its return link selects the current release. Align the versioned documentation and return link first. Four representative questions were answered and the default installation journey completed. Coverage comprises 12 source pages plus a rendered LTS Python page and a fetched release calendar; one non-default combination was exercised. Actual assistant citations, provider IP access and behavioral outcomes were not measured.

not_checked: Assumed English-speaking developers and analysts evaluating local analytical SQL, with macOS auto-detected in the browser; search locale was unknown.

Only the landing page, installation page and LTS Python documentation were rendered, at the default desktop viewport (screenshot 1280 x 720). Other clients, operating systems, releases and mobile layouts were not exercised.
Keyboard reachability, visible focus, contrast, complete accessibility conformance and performance metrics were not checked.

Six collector page records have capped evidence; absence claims are not made from those records. Eight collector requests were recorded as HTTP 308 errors; these were not classified as website defects. The browser successfully followed Get DuckDB to installation.

Four web-search queries were executed in one batch with an aggregated result pool; per-query ranks were not exposed or inferred. Foundation and GitHub are associated first-party sources; Amazon is an interested transaction counterparty, not an independent endorsement. No exhaustive reputation audit was performed.
Actual assistant answers/citations, authenticated flows, package installation, provider IP access, owner analytics and Search Console controls were not measured.
The collector's noindex candidate at /design was discarded because the inspected page is an explicit redirect stub pointing to /design/manual/, not an acquisition page exclusion.

findings.title: Python LTS documentation and its installation return route lose the selected release

evidence.observation: Rendered reproduction: Home > Get DuckDB > Python > 1.4.5 (LTS) produced /install/?platform=macos&environment=python&version=lts and pip install duckdb==1.4.5. Client documentation page opened /docs/lts/clients/python/overview, visibly labelled 1.4 LTS, but its Installation section used pip install duckdb. The same section's installation page link led to /install/?environment=python&platform=macos with 1.5.5 (current) selected and the unpinned command. Manually selecting 1.4.5 (LTS) recovered the pinned command. One of one non-default version handoffs tested was affected; the two affected page contexts are the LTS Python documentation and the returned installer. The source-fetch view also exposes the unpinned command on the LTS page.

suggested_action.summary: In the LTS Python Installation section, give the LTS-pinned command and include version=lts on its installation-page return link while retaining environment=python.
suggested_action.mechanism: Keeps a visitor's explicitly selected release consistent across instructions and the return to the installer, reducing the chance of following a different release's setup steps.
suggested_action.verification: Select Python and 1.4.5 (LTS), follow Client documentation page, confirm its installation instruction targets the LTS release, then follow installation page and verify Python plus LTS remain selected with the LTS-pinned command. Check the current-release route still gives its intended command.

readiness.detail: robots.txt returned 200. Its wildcard Allow: / permits all 12 collected URLs for named Googlebot, bingbot, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot and PerplexityBot policy checks; older /docs/1.3, /1.2, /1.1, /1.0 and /0.10 paths are disallowed. Training and user-fetch roles were recorded separately. No indexing/snippet restriction was observed on home or install. Policy permission is not verified provider access.

The home page's analytical SQL, in-process, file-format and license facts were available in both collected source text and rendered accessibility text. The untruncated source installer record contains selectors but no install command; the browser supplies the selected command, while the home page already supplies current install commands. No site-wide extraction failure is inferred. JSON-LD parsed without errors on the 12-page sample; home SoftwareApplication price 0 and MIT license agree with visible copy. Other structured values were not exhaustively checked.

All four questions, frozen after the landing-page inspection and before supporting-page judgment, have support for their required elements. The separate LTS continuity finding does not make the broader Python installation question unanswered.

The exact-entity, neutral task, current-release and governance queries returned the official site and related sources. Opened Foundation and GitHub pages agree on identity/license and product facts. Amazon's own acquisition announcement says the project remains under the independent Foundation and MIT license; this corroborates the transaction boundary from another entity but is an interested source. Wikipedia was opened as a lead and relies on the site's own sources for governance, so it was not treated as independent proof. No material contradiction was established in the checked claims.

Get DuckDB successfully reached a usable default macOS CLI installation command. Python and LTS controls changed the instruction and destination correctly; the subsequent LTS documentation/return sequence had the scoped friction documented in F-001. No consent overlay or challenge prevented the observed tasks.

evidence.quote: An analytical SQL database that can run in-process.
DuckDB was designed with both data science and data engineering workloads in mind.

intent_tests.reason: The landing page identifies analytical SQL, in-process deployment and relevant file formats; the inspected FAQ passage names data science and engineering audiences.

intent_tests.question: Is DuckDB free and open source, and who governs it?

evidence.quote: All components of DuckDB are available in the free version under this license
MIT-licensed, governed by the independent DuckDB Foundation.

intent_tests.reason: The quoted passages establish cost, license and governing entity, supported by the associated Foundation page.

intent_tests.question: What current stable version should a new user install?
intent_tests.reason: The rendered installer explicitly identifies current 1.5.5 and a macOS CLI instruction; the release calendar lists it as a past release and 1.5.6 as upcoming. No command was executed.

intent_tests.question: How does a Python user install and reach the matching client documentation?
intent_tests.reason: Selecting Python supplied its install command and a Python client documentation link. The link was followed after selecting LTS and reached Python API documentation. F-001 separately documents the version-specific instruction and return issue.
